talk: Is there a subject we keep avoiding? We don’t need to finish discussing it today; just say to each other: “I’m willing to find a time to face it together with you.”
When do you think we are most like “one new man,” united in heart and walking together?
acts: Take the initiative to remove one “brick”: talk through one small matter
Set a time with your spouse to face an avoided subject together
Each of you pray for one minute for your oneness
lessons.noon: “broke down the middle wall of separation” — Lord, right now tear down the wall I’ve built in my heart to protect myself.

lessons.title: Renewing Our Covenant Before the Lord
lessons.theme: Renew your covenant as a living sacrifice, and let Christ reign in your home

v: Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service.
Don’t be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, so that you may prove what is the good, well-pleasing, and perfect will of God.
What will I give to the LORD for all his benefits toward me?
I will take the cup of salvation, and call on the LORD’s name.
I will pay my vows to the LORD, yes, in the presence of all his people.

lessons.still: Recall the sound of your voice saying “I do” on your wedding day. How much did you understand then? And how much more grace have you experienced since? Quietly tell the Lord: “Lord, with the life I have today, I want to say ‘I do’ once more.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: This brings the mindset stage to a close. Change your mindset and your life will change; change your life and your daily living will change. Renewing our covenant turns these eight weeks of new thinking into the direction of our lives: life first, then relationship. Let Jesus reign in our home, let Jesus receive all the glory, and together build a household that belongs to God.
lessons.jesus: At the Last Supper, Jesus took the cup and said, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you” (Luke 22:20). He did not just speak this covenant; he kept it with his life. Our marriage covenant can hold, not because our willpower is strong enough, but because the Lord who made the new covenant lives in us.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, maker of the new covenant, thank you for making a covenant with us in your own blood and for keeping it faithfully. Today we once again present our bodies as a living sacrifice, and we offer our marriage to you anew. We will no longer live for ourselves; reign in our home and live in us. Strengthen our vows, so that together we may build a household that belongs to God and welcome your return. Amen.
teach: Most of us spoke our wedding vows amid excitement and nerves. Back then we didn’t really know which days “in good times and hard times” would include. Reading our vows again is not because the old covenant has expired, but because today we understand better what we are promising. It is like an old song: when you’re young, you sing the melody; after the years have passed, you sing your life.

Paul urges us “to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God” (Romans 12:1). Someone once said the trouble with a living sacrifice is that it keeps crawling off the altar, so it has to be offered again every day. The marriage covenant is the same: not a one-time declaration at a wedding, but a daily renewal for a lifetime. The psalmist asks, “What will I give to the LORD for all his benefits toward me?” (Psalm 116:12) And he answers: “I will pay my vows to the LORD, yes, in the presence of all his people” (Psalm 116:14). A vow is a response to grace.

Over these eight weeks, we started from God’s design and looked at the self-ruled life in Eden, at pride and humility, at self-denial and self-emptying. This time our vows carry something new: not only “I love you,” but “It is no longer I, but Christ in me who loves you.” If for now you can only walk this road alone, you can still say “I do” before the Lord first. And a clear reminder: covenant commitment never requires anyone to stay in violence or danger. If you have any concerns about your safety, seek help from a pastor and from professionals first.
q: Looking back over these eight weeks, which of my ideas about marriage has God changed?
If I were to read my vows again today, which line would I most want to say with a completely new heart?
talk: Over these eight weeks, what change or growth have you seen in me? Please affirm me specifically.
Before we renew our vows, is there anything you want to say to me first: thanks, an apology, or a hope? If your spouse can’t join you for now, write it as a short letter.
acts: Set a time and place this weekend to read your vows again
Write down the one line you most want to say to your spouse in your vows
Tell your spouse: “I do. I choose you again.”
lessons.noon: “present your bodies a living sacrifice” — Lord, right now I offer myself and our home to you once again.
